chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated that from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I entered upon Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام in his tent while he was speaking to a woman, so I hesitated before approaching him. He said: Come near; this is Umm Isma'il. She came, and I maintain that this is the place in which Allah nullified her hajj last year.

I had intended to enter ihram, so I said: Put water for me in the tent. The slave-girl took the water and placed it there, and I took advantage of her and had relations with her. Then I said: Wash your head and wipe it thoroughly in a way your mistress will not know. Then when you intend ihram, wash your body and do not wash your head, lest your mistress become suspicious.

Then she entered the tent of her mistress and went to take something, and her mistress touched her head and found the stickiness of water. So she shaved her head and beat her. Then I said to her: This is the place in which Allah nullified your hajj.

key_terms.اغْسِلِي: Wash; an imperative related to ritual washing.
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامَ: The state of consecration entered for hajj or 'umrah.
key_terms.الْجَارِيَةُ: The slave-girl mentioned in the narrative.
key_terms.الْخِبَاءِ: The tent or private enclosure in which the water was placed.
key_terms.جَسَدَكِ: Your body; mentioned in contrast to the head in the washing instructions.
key_terms.حَجَّهَا: Her hajj, which is said here to have been nullified.
key_terms.رَأْسَكِ: Your head; specifically mentioned regarding washing.

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith from al-Istibsar relate to ghusl al-janabah, ihram, and the invalidation of hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident connected to the rulings of ghusl al-janabah and the order of washing in relation to ihram and hajj. It illustrates how an improper act and its consequences led to the invalidation of the woman's hajj, within the legal discussion of ritual purity.
